chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Kansas City's big bands and clubs: Moten, Kirk, Pete Johnson, Joe Turner
summary: Taken to dances by his Uncle Charles, he heard the big bands and Pete Johnson, and Joe Turner was then a janitor at the Lone Star.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Oh. Well, who were the first musicians you ran into in Kansas City?
Oh, I used to go and listen to Benny Moten, Andy Kirk, --
Oh, you did? You heard everybody then.
Yeah, most all the big bands there.
Well, tell me.
George F. Lee and --
Oh, yeah. Well, you must have had a tremendous thrill when you arrived in Kansas City, a jumping town like that.
Oh, yeah. See, my uncle, he used to go to all the dances.
Oh, did he? Your father's brother?
My father's brother, my Uncle Charles.
Yeah.

And he would take me with him, because he knew I liked drums and all like that. And I would go to all the dances. And when I wasn't going to a dance, I was walking about in Kansas City, going to the--
In the street.
That's right, to the nightclubs.
That's where you first heard Pete Johnson, then.
Right, right.
Well, that was some piano playing, wasn't it?
Sure was. He certainly was.
And Joe Turner.
Well, Joe Turner wasn't singing when I came to Kansas City.
You really got there early, didn't you?
He was working as --
He was tending bar.
He was a janitor in the club. That's right.
Really? In that Sunset?
At the Lone Star.
Oh, really?
That's right.
He was the janitor.
He was the janitor there.
So he wasn't opening his mouth?
And they started letting him sing later on. He wanted to sit in, he'd learned all of the blues and those things.
Well, didn't he turn out to tend bar in the end?
Yeah, he was a bartender, turned out to tend bar and all that. But he was -- like I say, he was the janitor, cleaning up the place and like that.
But Pete was playing.
Pete was playing the piano, veah.
I think Pete was a wonderful piano player, don't you?
